documents.title: Follow-up - DM/HTN
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Turns 50 this week. DM/HTN check. Metformin daily. Admits he skips the BP pills when he leaves early for a job, which is most days - "maybe half the time." Has not checked sugars in months. Drinking - "less than before," won't put a number on it. Smoking unchanged. Did not go back to psychiatry.

No chest pain, no SOB, no headaches beyond his usual.

BP 148/94, recheck 146/92. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact.

A1c 7.4.

A/P
- HTN above goal, adherence is the issue rather than the regimen. Talked about taking both with the metformin at breakfast so they travel together. Pill box. Same doses.
- T2DM 7.4, drifting up. Metformin 1000 BID. Diet talk.
- Alcohol/tobacco - brief advice again, not ready.
- Shingles vaccine now that he's 50 - declines for now. FIT kit - declined, "later."

RTC 3-4 mo, physical in summer.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN NOTE (abbreviated)
Arrival 03/13/2025 17:40
51M with HTN, DM2, metabolic syndrome, tobacco and alcohol use.

CC: headaches in the morning, tired, short of breath with exertion.

HPI: Several months of dull headaches across both sides of the head, worst on waking, slowly getting worse. Also more winded on stairs than he used to be. No chest pain, palpitations, recent illness, visual change, dizziness or weakness. HTN for several years; has not kept up with follow-up. Reports taking only HCTZ and not every day. Eats a lot of salt. No regular exercise. 1 ppd. Drinks on weekends per pt.

VS: BP 188/106, P 84, RR 18.
Exam: Heart sounds normal. Mild crackles at both bases. Abdomen benign. Neuro nonfocal. Visual acuity normal. Fundi: arteriolar narrowing and AV nicking both eyes; no hemorrhage, exudate or disc swelling.
ECG and chest film: no acute findings.

Impression: Uncontrolled hypertension; hypertensive retinopathy.
Disposition: Discharged. Instructed to take lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide every day as prescribed, low-salt diet. Follow up with PCP within 1 week.

NKDA.

documents.title: Urgent Visit - Medications / Glucose
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in on a same-day slot after a text from his wife. First visit since 2/2024. ED in March for BP 188/106 with hypertensive retinopathy, then missed the follow-up.

He has not been taking the lisinopril or HCTZ - stopped after a few weeks following the ED, "felt fine." Takes metformin most days. Not checking sugars, meter is "somewhere." Smoking a pack a day, about 30 years. He says he knows he has to do something about his health. Not sure he can quit smoking or drop weight, has tried both. Wants to understand what each change would actually buy him and how hard it would be.

Labs 9/8: A1c 8.2, fasting glucose 176. TC 220, HDL 32, LDL 145, TG 250. Liver enzymes still up, similar to 2023. Kidney function and urine albumin normal.

Exam: BP 152/96. BMI 32. Acanthosis nigricans at the back and sides of the neck. Otherwise unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema, feet intact with normal monofilament.

A/P
1. Medication nonadherence / HTN uncontrolled. We went through what untreated pressure has already done to his eyes and can do to heart, brain and kidneys. Capacity: he can describe his conditions and the risks of leaving them untreated in his own words, weighs them against what he sees as the cost, and gives the same answer each time I come back to it - he has capacity to make these decisions, and his choice today is to restart both BP pills and see how it goes. Lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 re-sent.
2. T2DM, A1c 8.2 - poorly controlled with missed doses and diet. Metformin 1000 BID, every day. Restart fasting checks 3x/week.
3. Tobacco - long talk on the benefits (BP, heart, lungs, cost) and the hard parts (withdrawal, work breaks). Still not ready for patches or a pill; knows they're available. Lung cancer screening CT ordered.
4. Alcohol - AUDIT-C 6, says it's "down." Encouraged further cutback; psychiatry offer stands.
5. Weight/acanthosis - goes with the insulin resistance. Discussed realistic first steps.
6. Eyes - ophthalmology referral for the retinopathy and his diabetic eye exam.
7. Flu shot today. PHQ-9 4.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up for HTN/DM/metabolic syndrome after last fall's visit about missed meds. I was held up with an urgent add-on and he waited over an hour. Visibly angry when I came in, raised his voice - he's been waiting, nobody seems to care, he has a job to get to. I apologized, didn't argue, sat down, and let him finish. He calmed within a few minutes and stayed for the visit. No other complaints today.

Meds: taking metformin. Occasional ibuprofen for headaches. Not taking lisinopril or HCTZ again - ran out after the September fill and didn't call.

Labs 3/9: fasting glucose 158, A1c 7.8 (8.2 in Sept). Cr 1.2. UA no protein or blood.

BP 160/100, HR 88. Exam otherwise unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
1. Situational irritability/anger today, related to the wait. Resolved with acknowledgment. Will try to book him first slot of the day going forward.
2. HTN, uncontrolled, off meds again. Agrees to restart lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 today; refills sent. BMP 2 weeks after restarting (Cr 1.2 today).
3. T2DM, A1c 7.8. Metformin 1000 BID. Continue.
4. Tobacco/alcohol - he declined to get into it today; fair enough.
5. CT and eye referral still open - reminded.

RTC 1 month, first appointment of the morning.
